authorization.provenance: User to Codex after audit 119 and the README correction/disposition commit 459eda83.

scope: Accept S1-LL21-b and select one generated function per module with both B entry roles, at the reviewed measured engineering scope under benchmark policy v3.
exclusions: The current README corrects the eager-Liftoff retention figures to 458786 through 549124 bytes. The immutable R1 README preserves the stale r3 figures; replay R1 at ff3789f2.

Nineteen logical modules include two byte-identical binaries (twins_inner_2 and separate_inner_1), so the engine retains eighteen NativeModules. Distinct digests are not required; the duplicate benefits from the engine cache.

The roughly 1.93 ms cold figure measures decode/validation under the default lazy tier. Audit 119 observed roughly 8 ms with eager compilation in a separate three-process probe; neither is a comparative performance claim.
The three redefinitions change constants and retain equal encoded sizes. Different-body-shape revisions are not exercised.
Nineteen generated B modules, not the completed bootstrap closure. LL15 still determines final membership; no extrapolated boot-latency claim.
Expected inventory, ABI/layout versions and D2 classification are trusted build/owner inputs, not code signing.
Code IDs and slots are distinct concepts; this execution retains the inherited equal assignment and separately validates a non-equal permutation.
Owner binding selection and snapshot restoration are fixtures. Production symbol transactions stay with LL11-a; process/thread ownership and cross-dump remain separate slots.
Retain every old module and callable slot. This unit does not implement code reclamation, a merged fallback or a new lazy-loader profile.
Node default-tier timings are descriptive; eager Liftoff-only retention diagnostics are separate. No browser, JSPI, unshared runtime or speed-ranking claim.
Engine-reported NativeModule off-heap storage excludes shared WasmEngine overhead and is not an isolated executable-code size. Whole-process RSS is reported separately.
Full validated installation repeats digest/record checks and costs about 37 ms for the 19-module corpus; this cost is one-time loading, not arithmetic dispatch.
